generic: Oxytocics and Prostaglandin E1/E2 and Products for Cervical Dilatation
pharm: A class of uterotonics and cervical-ripening agents - oxytocin, prostaglandin E2 (dinoprostone), prostaglandin E1 analogue (misoprostol), and mechanical/osmotic dilators - used for cervical ripening, labor induction/augmentation, postpartum hemorrhage, and pregnancy termination.
quick: Varies by member (e.g., oxytocin 0.5-1 mU/min IV; dinoprostone 10 mg vaginal insert; misoprostol 25 mcg vaginal)
These agents ARE intended for use in pregnancy/labor (deliberate, monitored use)
Generally compatible (oxytocin promotes let-down; single peripartum doses acceptable)
Oxytocin - water intoxication risk; prostaglandins caution in impairment
Continuous fetal heart rate AND uterine activity monitoring
summary: This is a CLASS/GROUP entry covering uterotonics and cervical-ripening agents, not a single drug. It includes oxytocin (Pitocin; IV induction/augmentation and postpartum hemorrhage), dinoprostone (prostaglandin E2; Cervidil insert and Prepidil gel for cervical ripening), misoprostol (prostaglandin E1 analogue; off-label for cervical ripening, induction, and postpartum hemorrhage, and approved with mifepristone for medical abortion), and mechanical/osmotic cervical dilators (Foley balloon, laminaria, Dilapan-S). Oxytocin and dinoprostone are FDA-approved for obstetric use; misoprostol's obstetric uses are off-label. The principal hazard across the class is uterine tachysystole/hyperstimulation with fetal compromise, so continuous fetal heart rate and uterine activity monitoring is mandatory.
indications: Cervical ripening before labor induction (dinoprostone; misoprostol off-label; mechanical dilators)
Induction of labor (oxytocin; misoprostol off-label; mechanical dilators)
Prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage / uterine atony (oxytocin; misoprostol off-label)
Management of incomplete or inevitable abortion (oxytocin)
Medical abortion / early pregnancy loss (misoprostol combined with mifepristone)
Prevention of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers (misoprostol - its only FDA-approved indication)

dosage.t: Increase every 30-60 min until adequate contractions
dosage.n: >9-10 mU/min rarely needed at term; never give as undiluted IV bolus

dosage.d: 10-40 units in 1000 mL IV titrated, or 10 units IM
dosage.n: High-alert medication; do not give concentrated IV push
Remove at active labor, 12 h, or tachysystole; wait >=30 min before oxytocin

dosage.d: 0.5 mg, may repeat 0.5 mg every 6 h
dosage.n: Delay 6-12 h after last gel before starting oxytocin

dosage.d: 25 mcg vaginal q3-6h, or 25 mcg oral q2h
dosage.n: Avoid higher doses near term (tachysystole/rupture risk)

dosage.t: PPH single dose; abortion 24-48 h after mifepristone 200 mg PO
dosage.n: Heat-stable WHO essential uterotonic for PPH where oxytocin cold chain is unavailable

dosage.d: Foley balloon inflated 30-80 mL; osmotic dilators (laminaria, Dilapan-S)
dosage.t: Often placed overnight; ripens over hours
dosage.n: Preferred over prostaglandins with a prior cesarean (lower rupture risk)

admin: Oxytocin: infuse by pump, piggybacked into a mainline so it can be stopped instantly; never give a concentrated IV bolus
Cervidil: place transversely in the posterior vaginal fornix; keep patient recumbent ~2 hours; remove via the retrieval tape
Prepidil: allow to reach room temperature naturally; keep patient supine 15-30 minutes after instillation
Misoprostol: place the low-dose (25 mcg) tablet in the posterior fornix; avoid high doses near term
Use only ONE ripening/uterotonic modality at a time and respect washout intervals before starting oxytocin
moa: Oxytocin binds myometrial oxytocin receptors, raising intracellular calcium and producing rhythmic uterine contractions (and milk let-down). Dinoprostone (PGE2) ripens the cervix through collagen breakdown and softening with little uterotonic effect at ripening doses. Misoprostol (PGE1 analogue) softens the cervix and stimulates uterine contractions via prostaglandin receptors (and provides gastric cytoprotection in its approved use). Mechanical/osmotic dilators exert radial pressure and hygroscopic expansion, releasing endogenous prostaglandins and degrading cervical collagen.

absolute: Prior classical cesarean, major uterine surgery, or previous uterine rupture
Placenta or vasa previa / unexplained vaginal bleeding
relative: Prior low-transverse cesarean (mechanical preferred over prostaglandins)
Asthma, glaucoma, or significant cardiovascular/renal disease (prostaglandins)

preg: These agents are intended for use in pregnancy and labor; their obstetric use is deliberate and conducted under continuous monitoring. Misoprostol is teratogenic/abortifacient and is contraindicated in pregnancy when used for ulcer prevention.
lact: Generally compatible. Oxytocin promotes milk let-down and has minimal infant oral bioavailability; single peripartum doses of dinoprostone or misoprostol are rapidly cleared and generally considered compatible.
renal: Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect and can cause water intoxication, a risk that rises with impaired free-water clearance. Prostaglandins are metabolized hepatically, renally, and in the lung - use with caution in significant impairment (limited data).
hepatic: Caution in significant hepatic impairment (limited data) for the prostaglandin members; oxytocin is metabolized by the liver, placenta, and plasma oxytocinase.

major: Prostaglandins potentiate oxytocics - do NOT use simultaneously (additive tachysystole); observe washout intervals before oxytocin
Oxytocin with vasoconstrictors/sympathomimetics (with regional anesthesia) - severe hypertension
moderate: Oxytocin with cyclopropane or other anesthetics - hypotension and arrhythmia
interactions.diagnostics: Cardiotocography is used to detect tachysystole and fetal heart rate changes during administration.

serious: Uterine tachysystole/hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate abnormalities
emergency: Tachysystole with a non-reassuring fetal tracing

monitoring: Continuous electronic fetal heart rate monitoring whenever a uterotonic/prostaglandin is being given or an insert is in place
Continuous monitoring of uterine activity (tocodynamometry) - frequency, duration, and resting tone
Maternal vital signs and fluid balance (oxytocin water intoxication)
Availability of facilities for rapid cesarean delivery
counsel: You will be closely monitored; the medicine or insert is stopped or removed if contractions become too strong or the baby's heart rate is concerning
Stay recumbent after a Cervidil or Prepidil placement as directed
Report strong continuous pain, heavy bleeding, or leaking of fluid
Misoprostol use in labor/obstetrics is off-label; ask staff about expected cramping and diarrhea
With oxytocin, report headache or confusion (signs of fluid overload)
pk: Oxytocin IV ~1 min, IM 3-5 min; misoprostol-acid peaks ~30 min oral; dinoprostone over hours
Misoprostol-acid Tmax ~30 min; Cervidil releases ~0.3 mg/h
Oxytocin effect subsides ~1 h after stopping; cervical ripening over hours/overnight
Oxytocin refrigerate; Cervidil freezer -20 to -10 C; Prepidil 2-8 C; misoprostol room temp, dry
pearls: This is a class/group entry - oxytocin and dinoprostone are FDA-approved for obstetric use, whereas misoprostol's obstetric uses are off-label (only NSAID-ulcer prevention is approved; the abortion regimen is approved only with mifepristone)
Use only ONE ripening/uterotonic modality at a time and respect washout intervals (Cervidil 30 min, Prepidil 6-12 h, misoprostol ~4 h before oxytocin)
Tachysystole is defined as 6 or more contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes
Low-dose oxytocin (<=6 mU/min) mimics physiologic labor
Mechanical (Foley) ripening is preferred over prostaglandins in women with a prior cesarean (lower rupture risk)
Misoprostol is heat-stable, inexpensive, and a WHO essential uterotonic for PPH where the oxytocin cold chain is unavailable
missed: Not applicable in the usual sense - these are titrated, single-event, or scheduled obstetric interventions managed by the care team rather than patient self-administered scheduled doses.
overdose: Overdose presents as uterine tachysystole/hyperstimulation. Management: (1) stop the oxytocin infusion / remove the Cervidil insert / irrigate vaginal misoprostol / deflate or remove the balloon; (2) place the patient in left lateral decubitus, give maternal oxygen and IV fluids; (3) give a tocolytic such as terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneously (alternatively magnesium sulfate); (4) for oxytocin water intoxication, stop oxytocin, restrict fluids, cautiously correct hyponatremia, and manage seizures; (5) prepare for emergency cesarean if fetal status does not recover or rupture is suspected.
